# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhou_2026_nipocalimab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhou_2026_nipocalimab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70259> (open access; PMC13565270)
* Supplement: Supplemental Methods (model equations 1-5 and both parameter
  tables) accompanying the article.

Nipocalimab is an anti-FcRn monoclonal antibody. Zhou 2026 updated a
nipocalimab PK/FcRn-occupancy/IgG model, first developed in healthy volunteers,
with data from 14 pregnancies in the Phase 2 UNITY study of early-onset severe
hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN), adding time-varying body
weight (gestational weight gain) on clearance and central volume. The model
was then used to choose the Phase 3 dose (45 mg/kg IV weekly, dosed on current
body weight).

The model has three linked parts:

1. **PK and FcRn binding** -- a two-compartment model in which nipocalimab in
   serum binds FcRn at quasi-steady state (QSS); the drug-FcRn complex is
   internalised at `kint`, and the bindable FcRn pool turns over with
   synthesis `ksyn` and degradation `kdeg` (Supplement Equations 1-3).
2. **FcRn occupancy** -- percent unoccupied FcRn is free FcRn (including the
   fraction `1 - FR_R` that nipocalimab cannot reach) relative to the
   baseline total `R_total,0` (Equation 2).
3. **Total IgG** -- an indirect-response model in which FcRn-mediated
   recycling (`krec_IgG`) is scaled by the fraction of free bindable FcRn,
   so blocking FcRn raises the net IgG degradation rate (Equations 4-5).

# Population

The PK/FcRn-occupancy data set had 128 participants (114 healthy volunteers
and 14 pregnancies from 13 UNITY participants) with 1513 PK and 1209 FcRn
occupancy observations; the IgG data set had 144 participants (130 healthy
volunteers and the same 14 pregnancies) with 2110 observations (Zhou 2026
Table 1). Median age was 35 years (range 18-64), median body weight 70.5 kg
(50.3-110 kg), 66% were female, and the race distribution was 73.6% White,
18.8% Asian, 4.2% Black and 3.5% other; 36.8% were positive for antibodies to
nipocalimab. Healthy volunteers received single IV doses of 0.3-60 mg/kg (or
300 / 1200 mg) or 15 / 30 mg/kg IV weekly for four doses. In UNITY, pregnant
participants received 30 or 45 mg/kg IV weekly from gestational week 14 to 35,
dosed on baseline body weight or (in the last group) on current body weight
measured every 2 weeks.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zhou_2026_nipocalimab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. "PK
table" is the Supplement table "Parameter estimates for the final nipocalimab
HDFN PK model"; "IgG table" is "Parameter estimates for the final nipocalimab
HDFN PK-IgG model".

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL, 75 kg) | log(0.687 L/day) | PK table |
| `lvc` (Vc, 75 kg) | log(3.36 L) | PK table |
| `lq` (Q) | log(0.238 L/day) | PK table |
| `lvp` (Vp) | log(0.548 L) | PK table |
| `lFcRn0` (R_total,0) | log(135 nmol/L) | PK table |
| `lkss` (k_ss) | log(43.9 nmol/L) | PK table (footnote b: 6.23 ug/mL) |
| `lkint` (k_int) | log(65.6 1/day) | PK table |
| `lkdeg` (k_deg) | log(1.3 1/day), fixed | PK table ('FIX') |
| `FRmax` (FR_R) | 0.948 | PK table |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | PK table; Equation 3 |
| `lIgG0` (IgG baseline) | log(75.2 umol/L) | IgG table (footnote b: 11.3 g/L) |
| `lkdeg_IgG` | log(0.218 1/day) | IgG table |
| `lIgK` | log(4.90) | IgG table |
| IIV CL, Vc, R_total,0 | 20.6, 14.9, 21.3 %CV | PK table |
| IIV IgG baseline, k_deg_IgG | 22.7, 30.0 %CV | IgG table |
| `addSdELISA`, `addSdECLIA` | 0.424, 0.0306 nmol/L | PK table (ADD1 old assay, ADD2 new assay) |
| `propSd` | 0.141 | PK table (PROP RUV IV PK 14.1%) |
| `addSd_pctUnoccupiedFcRn`, `propSd_pctUnoccupiedFcRn` | 4.95 points, 0.241 | PK table (ADD / PROP RUV RO) |
| `addSd_IgG_obs`, `propSd_IgG_obs` | 4.13 umol/L, 0.079 | IgG table |
| Molecular weight | 142,000 g/mol | PK table footnote b |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)`, `d/dt(total_target)` | n/a | Supplement Equation 1 |
| QSS free concentration, complex, `R_total(0)`, % unoccupied | n/a | Supplement Equation 2 |
| `cl`, `vc` weight scaling | n/a | Supplement Equation 3 |
| `d/dt(total_igg)`, `ksyn_IgG` | n/a | Supplement Equation 4 |
| `krec_IgG = kdeg_IgG * IgK / (1 + IgK)` | n/a | Supplement Equation 5 |

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. Following the paper's simulation methods,
baseline body weight is drawn from a normal distribution with mean 66 kg and
SD 15 kg (truncated to 40-150 kg here). Body weight then increases linearly
through pregnancy by 0.59 kg/week, the slope of the "Adjusted from Hutcheon et
al. 2013" line in Supplemental Figure S2 (69 kg at gestational week 14 to
82 kg at week 36, digitised by the maintainers). Time zero is gestational
week 14; 22 weekly IV doses are given from week 14 to week 35 (day 147), and
follow-up continues to gestational week 40 (day 182). All simulated
pregnant participants use the electrochemiluminescence assay (`ELISA = 0`),
as in UNITY.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)

n_per_arm <- 200
gain_kg_per_day <- (82 - 69) / (36 - 14) / 7
dose_times <- (0:21) * 7
end_time <- 182
peak_offset <- 45 / 60 / 24 # Cmax sampled 45 min after the infusion (Methods)

bw_draw <- function(n) pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 66, 15), 40), 150)

# One regimen as a data frame of dose and observation rows. `basis` is
# "current" (dose on current weight) or "baseline" (dose on week-14 weight).
make_cohort <- function(n, mgkg, basis, regimen, obs_times, id_offset = 0L) {
  bw <- bw_draw(n)
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(i = seq_len(n), time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(
      id = ids[i],
      WT = bw[i] + gain_kg_per_day * time,
      amt = mgkg * (if (basis == "current") WT else bw[i]),
      evid = 1L,
      dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(i = seq_len(n), time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(
      id = ids[i],
      WT = bw[i] + gain_kg_per_day * time,
      amt = 0,
      evid = 0L,
      dvid = 1L
    )
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", ELISA = 0, regimen = regimen) |>
    select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, dvid, WT, ELISA, regimen) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

obs_fig2 <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, end_time, by = 1),
  dose_times[-1] - 0.001, # pre-dose troughs
  dose_times + peak_offset # 45-minute post-dose peaks
)))

events_fig2 <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_per_arm, 30, "baseline", "30 mg/kg on baseline weight", obs_fig2, 0L),
  make_cohort(n_per_arm, 45, "current", "45 mg/kg on current weight", obs_fig2, 1000L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_fig2[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

# Each dose is the nominal mg/kg times the weight it is based on: current
# weight in one regimen, the week-14 weight in the other.
dose_check <- events_fig2 |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(
    on_current = max(abs(amt / WT - amt[1] / WT[1])),
    on_baseline = max(abs(amt - amt[1])),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
stopifnot(
  all(dose_check$on_current[dose_check$regimen == "45 mg/kg on current weight"] < 1e-8),
  all(dose_check$on_baseline[dose_check$regimen == "30 mg/kg on baseline weight"] < 1e-8),
  # first doses differ between participants (one per sampled body weight)
  length(unique(events_fig2$amt[events_fig2$evid == 1 & events_fig2$time == 0])) > 300
)
```

# Simulation

Observation rows use the `central` state plus `dvid = 1`: the model declares
three endpoints (`Cc`, `pctUnoccupiedFcRn`, `IgG_obs`), and every endpoint is
returned as a column on every observation row.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Zhou_2026_nipocalimab")
stopifnot(identical(
  rxode2::rxode(mod)$state,
  c("central", "peripheral1", "total_target", "total_igg")
))

sim_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_fig2,
  keep = c("regimen", "WT"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(igg_cfb = 100 * (IgG_obs / first(IgG_obs) - 1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(ga_week = 14 + time / 7)
```

# Replicate Figure 2

Panel (a): serum nipocalimab concentration on a log scale with the 1-10 ug/mL
band the paper shades as the concentrations corresponding to full FcRn
occupancy. The 45-minute post-dose peaks and pre-dose troughs are included in
the sampling grid.

```{r figure-2a}
# Replicates Figure 2a of Zhou 2026: median and 90% prediction interval.
sim_fig2 |>
  group_by(regimen, ga_week) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q50 = median(Cc), q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(q05, q50, q95), \(x) pmax(x, 0.01))) |>
  ggplot(aes(ga_week, q50, colour = regimen, fill = regimen)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 1, ymax = 10,
           fill = "khaki", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 35, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.01, 3000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Gestational age (weeks)", y = "Nipocalimab concentration (ug/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2a of Zhou 2026 (values below 0.01 ug/mL drawn at 0.01)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Panels (b) and (c): percent unoccupied FcRn and percent change from baseline
in total serum IgG, on a daily grid.

```{r figure-2bc, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figures 2b and 2c of Zhou 2026: median and 90% prediction interval.
sim_fig2 |>
  filter(time == round(time)) |>
  select(regimen, ga_week, pctUnoccupiedFcRn, igg_cfb) |>
  pivot_longer(c(pctUnoccupiedFcRn, igg_cfb), names_to = "endpoint") |>
  group_by(regimen, ga_week, endpoint) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(value, 0.05),
    q50 = median(value),
    q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(endpoint = factor(
    endpoint,
    levels = c("pctUnoccupiedFcRn", "igg_cfb"),
    labels = c("FcRn unoccupied receptor (%)", "Serum IgG change from baseline (%)")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(ga_week, q50, colour = regimen, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 35, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Gestational age (weeks)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figures 2b and 2c of Zhou 2026."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The paper reports a sustained 80-85% reduction of maternal IgG during
treatment, full FcRn blockade at weekly troughs, elimination of nipocalimab
within 1-2 weeks of the last dose, and IgG recovery toward baseline within
about 5 weeks of the last dose.

```{r figure-2-checks}
on_treatment <- sim_fig2 |>
  filter(time >= 35, time <= 147) |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(
    igg_cfb = mean(igg_cfb),
    unocc = max(pctUnoccupiedFcRn[time %in% (dose_times[-1] - 0.001)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    median_igg_cfb = median(igg_cfb),
    median_max_trough_unoccupied = median(unocc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(on_treatment, digits = 1,
             caption = "Gestational weeks 19-35: median IgG change from baseline and median worst-trough percent unoccupied FcRn.")

stopifnot(
  # Paper: 80-85% IgG reduction during treatment with both regimens.
  all(on_treatment$median_igg_cfb < -75 & on_treatment$median_igg_cfb > -90),
  # Paper Figure 2b: about 5% unoccupied FcRn (the unreachable 1 - FR_R) at
  # weekly troughs for the 45 mg/kg current-weight regimen.
  on_treatment$median_max_trough_unoccupied[
    on_treatment$regimen == "45 mg/kg on current weight"] < 10
)
```

# Replicate Table 2: dosing delays

Table 2 of Zhou 2026 gives the simulated percentage of pregnant participants
with full FcRn occupancy for 15, 30, 45 and 60 mg/kg weekly (dosed on current
weight) when a dose is delayed by 0-3 days. The paper does not state the exact
criterion; here full occupancy is taken as a trough concentration at or above
the 10 ug/mL FcRn blockade threshold quoted in the Results, evaluated when the
dose after gestational week 35 is delayed by 0, 1, 2 or 3 days (the end of
treatment, when weight gain is largest).

```{r table-2}
delay_obs <- 147 + 7 + 0:3
events_tab2 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(15, 30, 45, 60)), function(k) {
  mgkg <- c(15, 30, 45, 60)[k]
  make_cohort(n_per_arm, mgkg, "current", paste(mgkg, "mg/kg"), delay_obs,
              id_offset = 2000L + (k - 1L) * 1000L)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_tab2[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_tab2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events_tab2, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame"
)

published_tab2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~delay, ~published,
  "15 mg/kg", 0, 47,    "15 mg/kg", 1, 24.4, "15 mg/kg", 2, 11.3, "15 mg/kg", 3, 4.7,
  "30 mg/kg", 0, 99.1,  "30 mg/kg", 1, 96.3, "30 mg/kg", 2, 86.1, "30 mg/kg", 3, 71,
  "45 mg/kg", 0, 99.9,  "45 mg/kg", 1, 99.8, "45 mg/kg", 2, 98.4, "45 mg/kg", 3, 95.5,
  "60 mg/kg", 0, 100,   "60 mg/kg", 1, 99.9, "60 mg/kg", 2, 99.8, "60 mg/kg", 3, 98.8
)

tab2 <- sim_tab2 |>
  mutate(delay = time - 154) |>
  group_by(regimen, delay) |>
  summarise(simulated = 100 * mean(Cc >= 10), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(published_tab2, by = c("regimen", "delay"))

tab2 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen (weekly IV)" = regimen,
    "Dosing delay (days)" = delay,
    "Simulated % with trough >= 10 ug/mL" = simulated,
    "Zhou 2026 Table 2 (%)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Replicates Table 2 of Zhou 2026.")

sim_pct <- function(r, d) tab2$simulated[tab2$regimen == r & tab2$delay == d]
stopifnot(
  # 45 mg/kg keeps nearly everyone covered without a delay (paper 99.9%).
  sim_pct("45 mg/kg", 0) > 95,
  # A 3-day delay at 45 mg/kg still covers most participants (paper 95.5%).
  sim_pct("45 mg/kg", 3) > 80,
  # 15 mg/kg loses coverage in most participants after a 3-day delay
  # (paper 4.7%).
  sim_pct("15 mg/kg", 3) < 20
)
```

The simulated percentages follow the paper's pattern: coverage falls quickly
with each day of delay below 45 mg/kg, while 45 and 60 mg/kg stay above 90%
after a 3-day delay; at 45 and 60 mg/kg the simulated and published values
agree within a few points. At the lower doses the simulated coverage is
lower than the paper's (by about 6-10 points at 30 mg/kg with a delay and
by up to about 15 points at 15 mg/kg without one). These regimens sit on the
steep part of the TMDD curve, where coverage is very sensitive to choices
the paper does not report: the exact occupancy criterion, the dosing
interval at which the delay was applied, and the per-individual spread of
gestational weight gain. With 200 participants per regimen the Monte Carlo
standard error is also about 3.5 percentage points near 50%.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA table. Supplemental Figure S3 (reprinted from the
UNITY publication) shows the observed median serum concentrations by regimen;
the maintainers read the week-35 post-infusion peak and the week-34 pre-dose
trough from that figure for the two regimens simulated above (approximate,
+/- about 25 ug/mL given the figure's resolution; n = 3 and 4 participants).
The simulation gives doses as IV bolus, so `cmax` is the concentration at the
start of the final dosing interval and slightly overstates a sample taken
45 minutes after an infusion.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_fig2 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 140, time < 154) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)

dose_nca <- events_fig2 |>
  filter(evid == 1, time >= 140) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | regimen + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(140, 147),
  end = c(147, 154),
  cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  cmin = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cmax, ~cmin,
  "30 mg/kg on baseline weight", 655, 25,
  "45 mg/kg on current weight", 1110, 220
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "regimen",
  params = c("cmax", "cmin"),
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", cmin = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated median (weeks 34-35) vs. observed median read from Supplemental Figure S3. * differs from the observed value by >20%."
)

sim_trough <- sim_fig2 |>
  filter(time == 147 - 0.001) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(trough = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(
  # Structural check against the observed week-34 trough in the
  # current-weight group (~220 ug/mL): a mis-scaled CL, Vc or dose moves
  # this by far more than 50%.
  abs(log(sim_trough$trough[sim_trough$regimen == "45 mg/kg on current weight"] / 220)) < log(1.5)
)
```

```{r trough-30}
trough_30 <- sim_fig2 |>
  filter(time == 147 - 0.001, regimen == "30 mg/kg on baseline weight") |>
  pull(Cc)
```

The 45 mg/kg current-weight regimen reproduces the observed peak and trough
within about 20%. In the 30 mg/kg baseline-weight group the simulated median
week-34 trough (`r signif(median(trough_30), 2)` ug/mL) is about three times
the observed median read from Figure S3 (about 25 ug/mL, n = 3); the
simulated 5th percentile is `r signif(quantile(trough_30, 0.05), 2)` ug/mL and
`r round(100 * mean(trough_30 < 10), 1)`% of simulated participants fall below
10 ug/mL. Troughs at this dose sit on the steep, target-mediated part of the
concentration curve, where a small difference in effective mg/kg moves the
trough several-fold, and the observed median comes from three participants
read off a figure near its axis. The paper's Results likewise state that
simulations of this regimen put troughs below the 10 ug/mL threshold with
gestational weight gain, and Figure 2a of the paper shows observed troughs of
roughly 20-60 ug/mL in this group late in pregnancy.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Free-FcRn fraction driving IgG recycling.** Supplement Equation 4 defines
  `F_free` as free FcRn at time t over the free FcRn "that can bind to
  nipocalimab and IgG" at time 0. The model uses free *bindable* FcRn,
  `(R_total - RC) / (R_total,0 * FR_R)`, which reaches 0 at full blockade --
  the condition under which Equation 5 states the minimal IgG fraction is
  `1 / (1 + IgK)`. The observed percent unoccupied FcRn instead includes the
  unbindable fraction `1 - FR_R` (Equation 2) and floors near 5%.
- **FcRn synthesis rate.** `Ksyn` is described only as "determined by kdeg and
  R_total at baseline". It is set to `kdeg * R_total,0 * FR_R`, which holds
  the bindable pool at its Equation 2 initial value `R_total(0)` before
  dosing.
- **Occupancy endpoint.** The residual-error rows are labelled "RO" in the
  supplement; they are applied to percent unoccupied FcRn, the quantity
  plotted in Figure 2b. A 24.1% proportional error is plausible for a
  quantity near 5% but not for an occupancy near 95%.
- **Observed concentration.** `Cc` is the total (free + FcRn-bound)
  nipocalimab concentration, the C_total of Equation 1, and the model is
  dosed in mg with concentrations in ug/mL. FcRn parameters stay in nmol/L
  as estimated and are converted with the 142,000 g/mol molecular weight
  given in the supplement; the additive PK residual SDs (reported in nmol/L)
  are converted the same way inside `model()`.
- **Assay.** The ELISA ("old assay") additive residual applies to three
  healthy-volunteer studies; the electrochemiluminescence assay ("new
  assay") applies to UNITY and NCT04848558. Simulations of pregnancy use
  `ELISA = 0`.
- **IIV.** The supplement reports IIV as %CV; variances were computed as
  `log(CV^2 + 1)`. No correlations between random effects were reported.
- **Infusion duration.** Not reported; doses are simulated as IV bolus.
- **Weight gain.** Linear 0.59 kg/week for every participant, from the
  Hutcheon-based line in Supplemental Figure S2; the paper's simulation drew
  weight gain from a distribution whose spread is not reported. The UNITY
  protocol re-weighed participants every 2 weeks; the simulation uses
  current weight at each dose.
- **Exposure-response.** The exploratory exposure-response analysis
  (Figure 3, Table S1) reports tertile rates only, with no fitted model, and
  is not part of this model.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-11-17.
